If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early-horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for pessimism.  
If sentiment swings sharply (≥0.67 then ≤0.33 or vice versa) within last 5 days, apply a 2–3% downward correction to forecast at day 15 to dampen volatility bias.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) across last 5 days and forecast shows strong upward trend, reduce slope by 0.5–1.0% per day in late-horizon (days 20–30) to prevent overcorrection.  
If sentiment is positive but forecast is below historical mean for 3 consecutive days, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias in late-horizon to align with sentiment momentum.  
If sentiment is negative and forecast is above historical mean for 3 consecutive days, apply 0.5–1.0% downward bias in early-horizon to reflect sentiment reversal.
